input: nums is an Array of n integers in [-1000000,1000000], with 0 <= n <=2000. Integer inputs, when present, are primitive safe-integer Numbers excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, proxies, subclasses or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: Boolean indicating whether there exist indices i,j,k with 0<i, i+1<j, j+1<k and k<n-1 such that the four NONEMPTY segments nums[0:i], nums[i+1:j], nums[j+1:k] and nums[k+1:n] have equal sums. The three cut elements nums[i], nums[j], nums[k] are excluded. Fewer than seven elements return false.
mutation_aliasing: All input values, caller containers and ordering remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state and separate calls share no mutable result state. A private prefix-sum Array and one private set per middle cut are allocated. No input segment is sliced or removed.
numeric: Prefix sums lie within +/-2000000000; differences of these prefixes conservatively lie within +/-4000000000 and are exact safe integers. Every endpoint and n+1 prefix length is small. Negative values and zero sums are supported; positivity is not assumed.
complexity: O(n^2+1) time under average constant set operations and O(n+1) live prefix/set storage. For each middle cut, record equal left-pair sums then seek an equal right-pair sum. Across middle cuts O(n^2+1) set entries may be allocated in total, but only one middle-cut set remains live. Map/set operation costs assume ordinary average O(1) lookup; target-runtime behavior must be qualified, and universal ECMAScript constant-time guarantees or adversarial collision resistance are not claimed.
